correctness.rationale: Exact rank-three parity-check classification gives 30 shortened-Hamming diagonal cores; 512 exhaustive cosets per core and the weight(t)+2weight(restriction) identity show exactly 72 admissible one-dimensional extensions per core. The three polynomial distributions count 48/16/8 cosets, giving 2160 distinct codes. The standalone verifier independently exhausts every coset and labeled core. A self-contained Griesmer–MacWilliams contradiction excludes any [12,5,5] linear code; a doubled core plus (111111,000000) realizes dimension 4 and distance 6. The theorem is finite and no extrapolation is made.

value.rationale: The classified family is exactly the first length-12 d=5 finite instance of the higher-distance diagonal-coherence question posed as Problem 6.30 of arXiv:2610.33676. Counting all 2160 optimal labeled subspaces and distinguishing three full weight enumerators provides nontrivial structural data beyond a routine existence check or parameter-table lookup. The result answers this natural bounded case while explicitly leaving general d and m open.
